summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Layer 1B expansion found one reference leader and three discovery-lane companies with direct or second-order exposure to data-center-driven behind-the-meter gas generation. GE Vernova anchors the turbine-slot scarcity thesis. INNIO is newly US-listed and unusually pure in distributed gas engines for data centers. Power Solutions International is a smaller, underfollowed emissions-certified engine/power-systems supplier with stated data-center demand. CECO Environmental is a second-order emissions/noise-control supplier tied to natural-gas power generation supporting data-center expansion. No trading recommendation is implied. Expanded the universe around the behind-the-meter gas-power node with one direct turbine reference name and three underfollowed second-order public suppliers. The evidence supports a real chokepoint setup: GE Vernova reports gas-power backlog and slot reservations expanding from 83 GW to 100 GW in Q1 2026, while Baker Hughes has a direct 2026 order for gas turbines and generator equipment for U.S. data-center power projects. The underfollowed lane should focus less on hyperscaler headlines and more on turbine/generator packages, off-grid natural-gas EPC, emissions/noise controls, power conversion, and integration services. Expanded universe for the behind-the-meter gas-power node. The core chokepoint hypothesis remains plausible: AI/data-center load growth is pushing operators toward on-site or near-site gas generation, creating demand for scarce turbine slots, packaged generators, distributed-power fleets, gas-compression services, switchgear/enclosur
